brief: Tonight is Push A, and it is the same Push A I wrote up yesterday. You did not log a session last night and nothing new has landed since the Legs B on Thursday 17 September, so almost every number on this card is unchanged on purpose. Re-deriving your numbers off evidence I have already read is how this review used to hand you a different answer every morning, and I am not doing that. One number did move, and you should hear why before you see it. Yesterday's crossover card told you the 17.5 you handled on 27 August was the old gym's pulley and does not transfer — and then, in the same sentence, asked for 15 reps on all three sets because you did exactly that on 17 August. 17 August was that same old gym. The card threw the old gym out for the weight and leaned on it for the reps, and it cannot have it both ways. What the log actually shows: on 17 August, old gym, at these exact dial numbers, you did 15, 15 and 15. On 8 September, new gym, at the same dial numbers, you did 14, 13 and 13. Same numbers on the machine, fewer reps — the new pulley is harder. So the target drops to 15, 14 and 13: one more rep on the first set, one more on the second, level with your best on the third. The weights are untouched. Everything else stands. Incline press: open at 155 for 8, which you own, then three sets at 160 starting at 6 reps. Know going in that the fourth set is one you have not done since the move — 8 September was three sets, not four. Chest press: 150 for 12, then 157.5 for 12 twice, and the 165 from 14 September is still not being carried over, because that machine is in your other gym. While I am correcting things, that session read 160 for 10, then 165 for 10 and 165 for 9 — not 165 for 10 twice, which is what got repeated back to you. Shoulder press stays at 45 and the job is 10 reps on all three. Reverse pec deck: 100 for 13, three sets. Overhead triceps: 55 for 12, 11 and 10, and the third set is the entire point of the lift right now. Rope pushdown holds at 45 for 14 and 14 — and the second 14 is the hard half, because since July your second set has come in under your first every single time. Two things outside the gym. Nobody has weighed you since 23 August, 207 lb, twenty-seven days ago, with the show 163 days out. And there is exactly one cardio session in your entire log — 15 minutes on the elliptical on 21 July. If conditioning is happening it is not being recorded, and if it is not happening, that is the gap I would close first. Last thing: this is the end of the block. Tonight and tomorrow are your last two hard sessions. The deload starts Monday 21 September at lighter loads and fewer sets.

flags.note: No Push A was logged last night, so this card is the same one that was waiting for you yesterday. Nothing new has been logged since Thursday 17 September.

One number changed from yesterday: the cable crossover asks 15, 14, 13 instead of 15, 15, 15. Yesterday's card refused the old gym's weight and then used the old gym's reps in the same sentence. At these same dial numbers you did 15/15/15 at the old gym on 17 August and 14/13/13 at this gym on 8 September.
Rope pushdown asks 45 for 14 and 14. The second 14 is the harder half: since July your second set has landed under your first on every single session.
The fourth set of incline press is one you have not done since changing gyms — 8 September was three sets. It is what the program asks for; just do not be surprised by it.

Last week of Meso 2. Tonight and tomorrow are your final two hard sessions; the deload runs Monday 21 September to Sunday 27 September at lighter loads and fewer sets. Next in rotation after tonight is Pull A.
No bodyweight since 23 August — 207 lb, twenty-seven days ago, with the show 163 days out. It is the one number none of us can estimate for you.
Your log contains exactly one cardio entry ever: 15 minutes on the elliptical, 21 July. Either conditioning is not being recorded or it is not happening, and with a March show both of those matter.

Push A still has no direct side-delt work — you removed the cable lateral raise on 14 September and the only laterals left are on Push B. Nobody has decided whether that is what you want with a show in March. This is deliberately not a Yes/No card, because putting one in front of you would reverse your own recent answer with nothing new behind it. Tell me if you want it back.

Your recovery trainer read all twenty-nine of your notes directly this morning and none of them report pain, soreness, joint trouble or injury. It had to read them by hand because the automatic pain list is still broken — its only ever entry is your 23 August lateral-raise sentence, matched because 'number' contains 'numb'. Fixing that needs a code change I am not allowed to make.

Still open from 14 September: you accepted the Push B overhead press going to dumbbells and the pec deck dropping to two sets, then started that session under three minutes later and the app handed you the old card. The change is in force now, but it has never actually been tried, and it will be Push B before that gets tested.
Three trainers reported. One disagreement, settled for the recovery seat on the cable crossover. No vetoes, and nobody raised a pain or injury objection.

proposals.why: Overhead cable triceps is the last lift that is identical on both push days — three sets of 10 to 12, run at 55 pounds on 8 September and again at 55 on 14 September, finishing on 9 reps under the bottom of the range both nights; this takes Push B to 8 to 10 so the two days stop being the same set, the way your chest press already splits.

dissent.progression: Hold the weights and ask 15 on all three — he completed exactly that at exactly these loads on 17 August, so it is a repeat, not a reach.
dissent.recovery: Same weights, but 15, 14, 13 — he has never produced three flat sets of 15 at this gym, and both readings here decayed inside the session.
dissent.why: I checked the 17 August session myself and it is the old gym — the same old gym whose 17.5 the card refuses to carry across one clause earlier. You cannot discard a building for the weight and cite it for the reps. Strip the old gym out and the only evidence that survives is 8 September at this gym: 14, 13, 13 at these same dial numbers, against 15, 15, 15 at the old one. Same numbers on the machine, fewer reps, which says this pulley is heavier. Recovery's 15/14/13 is a step up on the first two sets and level on the third, it prescribes nothing below what he has done here, and it is the only version of this card that does not contradict itself.

overrides.reason: On 8 September you hit 155 for 8, 8 and 8 with the barbell — the top of the range on every set, minutes apart — so this is your earned step: open at 155, then three sets at 160 from 6 reps. Four sets tonight; the fourth is one you have not done since the gym change.

Your opener earned a step because 142.5 for 12 on 8 September is the top of the range, but the 157.5 sets gave 11 and 10 and stay. The 165 from 14 September is deliberately not carried across: that night's machines were dialled in kilos and its overhead slot was a barbell, so it is a different room and a machine number does not cross rooms.

Weights unchanged, target corrected. At these same dial numbers you did 15, 15, 15 at the old gym on 17 August and 14, 13, 13 here on 8 September — so this pulley is harder and importing the old gym's reps was wrong. Tonight is 15, 14, 13: one better on the first set, one better on the second, level with your best on the third.

A 45-lb dumbbell weighs the same in any building, and 8s became 9s between 27 August and 8 September — real progress, but not enough to earn the 50s. What moved is the target, because you accepted the 10-to-12 range on 17 September, so the ask is 10 on all three.

In this room you have read 13 reps once at 100 and 12 every other set, so the weight cannot move — the ask is 13 on all three, one past anything you have completed at this load, and three sets because 8 September stopped at two.

Two sessions six days apart tell the same story at 55 — 11, 10, 9 and then 12, 10, 9 — so the load stays and the third set is the whole target. Ten reps on it is the first thing this lift has to prove.

The cut to 45 on 8 September did its job — 13 and 12 put both sets inside the range for the first time since July — so the weight holds and the reps climb to 14 on both. The second one is the hard half: your set two has come in under your set one every session since July.
